verses.1:1: The word of the LORD which came to Micah the Moreshite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he beheld concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: Hear, all you peoples; give ear, O earth, and all that fills it! Let the Lord GOD be a witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.
verses.1:3: For behold, the LORD is coming forth from His place; He will descend and tread upon the high places of the earth.
verses.1:4: The mountains shall melt beneath Him, and the valleys shall be split apart, like wax before the fire, like waters poured down a steep descent.
verses.1:5: All this is because of the transgression of Jacob and because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem?
verses.1:6: Therefore I will make Samaria a heap of ruins in the open field, places for planting a vineyard; I will pour down her stones into the valley, and I will lay bare her foundations.
verses.1:7: All her carved images shall be beaten to pieces, all her hires shall be burned with fire, and all her idols I will lay desolate; for from the hire of a harlot she gathered them, and to the hire of a harlot they shall return.
verses.1:8: Because of this I will lament and wail; I will go barefoot and naked; I will raise a lamentation like the jackals and a mourning like the ostriches.
verses.1:9: For her wound is incurable; for it has come even to Judah; it has reached to the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem.
verses.1:10: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all! In Beth-le-aphrah, roll yourself in the dust.
verses.1:11: Pass on your way, O inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame! The inhabitant of Zaanan does not go forth; the lamentation of Beth-ezel shall take away from you its standing place.
verses.1:12: For the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good, because calamity has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.1:13: Harness the chariot to the swift steeds, O inhabitant of Lachish—she was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.
verses.1:14: Therefore you shall give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib shall prove a deception to the kings of Israel.
verses.1:15: Yet again I will bring a conqueror against you, O inhabitant of Mareshah; the glory of Israel shall come even to Adullam.
verses.1:16: Make yourself bald and shear your head for the children of your delight; widen your baldness like the vulture, for they have gone into exile from you.
verses.2:1: Woe to those who devise iniquity and plot evil upon their beds! At the light of morning they carry it out, because it is in the power of their hand.
verses.2:2: They covet fields and seize them by violence, and houses, and carry them off; thus they oppress a man and his household, a man and his inheritance.
verses.2:3: Therefore thus says the LORD: "Behold, against this family I am devising calamity, from which you shall not remove your necks; nor shall you walk haughtily, for it shall be a time of calamity."
verses.2:4: In that day one shall take up a taunt against you and wail with a bitter lamentation, saying, "We are utterly ruined! He changes the portion of my people; how He removes it from me! To the rebellious He divides our fields!"
verses.2:5: Therefore you shall have no one to cast the measuring line by lot in the assembly of the LORD.
verses.2:6: "Do not prophesy!" thus they prophesy. They shall not prophesy of these things; disgrace shall not depart.
verses.2:7: Should it be said, O house of Jacob, "Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient? Are these His doings?" Do not My words do good to him who walks uprightly?
verses.2:8: Lately My people have risen up like an enemy; you strip the splendid robe from off the garment of those who pass by securely, as men returning from war.
verses.2:9: The women of My people you drive out from their pleasant houses; from their little children you take away My splendor forever.
verses.2:10: Arise and depart, for this is not the resting place; because of uncleanness it shall bring destruction, even a grievous destruction.
verses.2:11: If a man walking in wind and falsehood should tell lies, saying, "I will prophesy to you of wine and strong drink," he would be the very prophet for this people!
verses.2:12: I will surely assemble all of you, O Jacob; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel. I will set them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the midst of its pasture; they shall resound loudly because of men.
verses.2:13: The one who breaks through goes up before them; they break through, pass through the gate, and go out by it; their king passes on before them, with the LORD at their head.
verses.3:1: And I said: "Hear now, O heads of Jacob, and you rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice?
verses.3:2: You who hate good and love evil, who tear their skin from off them and their flesh from off their bones,
verses.3:3: who also eat the flesh of my people, flay their skin from off them, shatter their bones, and chop them up as for the pot, like meat within a cauldron.
verses.3:4: Then they shall cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them; He will even hide His face from them at that time, because they have made their deeds evil."
verses.3:5: Thus says the LORD: "Concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who bite with their teeth and cry, 'Peace!'—yet against him who puts nothing into their mouths they consecrate war:
verses.3:6: therefore it shall be night to you without vision, and it shall be darkness to you without divination. The sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall grow dark over them.
verses.3:7: The seers shall be put to shame, and the diviners confounded; indeed, they shall all cover their lips, for there is no answer from God."
verses.3:8: But as for me, I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
verses.3:9: Hear this now, O heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who abhor justice and pervert all that is upright,
verses.3:10: who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity.
verses.3:11: Her heads judge for a bribe, her priests give instruction for a price, and her prophets practice divination for silver; yet they lean upon the LORD, saying, "Is not the LORD in our midst? No calamity shall come upon us."
verses.3:12: Therefore, on account of you, Zion shall be plowed like a field, Jerusalem shall become heaps of ruins, and the mountain of the house like the wooded heights.
verses.4:1: And it shall come to pass in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be firmly established at the summit of the mountains, and it shall be lifted up above the hills; and peoples shall stream to it.
verses.4:2: And many nations shall come and say, "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob, so that He may instruct us in His ways, and that we may walk in His paths." For from Zion the law shall go forth, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.4:3: He shall judge between many peoples and render decisions for mighty nations afar off; they shall hammer their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn warfare anymore.
verses.4:4: And every man shall sit beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, with no one to make them afraid; for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
verses.4:5: For all the peoples walk, every one in the name of his god; yet we shall walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
verses.4:6: "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will gather the lame, and assemble the outcast, even those whom I have afflicted.
verses.4:7: And I will make the lame a remnant, and the one cast far off a mighty nation; and the LORD shall reign over them on Mount Zion from this time forth and forevermore."
verses.4:8: And as for you, O tower of the flock, stronghold of the daughter of Zion, to you it shall come; indeed, the former dominion shall return, the kingdom to the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.4:9: Now why do you cry out aloud? Is there no king in your midst? Has your counselor perished, that anguish has seized you like a woman in labor?
verses.4:10: Writhe and strain in labor, O daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth; for now you shall go forth from the city and dwell in the open field, and you shall go as far as Babylon. There you shall be delivered; there the LORD shall redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
verses.4:11: And now many nations have assembled against you, saying, "Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gloat over Zion."
verses.4:12: Yet they do not know the thoughts of the LORD, nor do they discern His counsel; for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
verses.4:13: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion; for I will make your horn iron, and I will make your hooves bronze. You shall crush many peoples in pieces, and I will devote their gain to the LORD, and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
verses.4:14: Now muster yourself in troops, O daughter of troops; he has laid siege against us. With a rod they shall strike the judge of Israel upon the cheek.
verses.5:1: Yet you, O Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the thousands of Judah, out of you shall come forth for Me One who shall be Ruler in Israel, whose goings forth are from ancient times, from the days of eternity.
verses.5:2: Therefore He shall give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth; then the rest of His brethren shall return to the children of Israel.
verses.5:3: And He shall stand and shepherd in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD His God; and they shall abide, for now He shall be great even to the ends of the earth.
verses.5:4: And this One shall be peace. When the Assyrian comes into our land, and when he treads in our citadels, then we shall raise up against him seven shepherds and eight princes of men.
verses.5:5: They shall shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod at its entrances; thus He shall deliver us from the Assyrian when he comes into our land and when he treads within our borders.
verses.5:6: Then the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers upon the grass, which does not wait for man, nor tarry for the sons of men.
verses.5:7: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which, when it passes through, tramples down and tears in pieces, and there is no one to deliver.
verses.5:8: Your hand shall be lifted high over your adversaries, and all your enemies shall be cut off.
verses.5:9: "And it shall come to pass in that day," declares the LORD, "that I will cut off your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots.
verses.5:10: I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
verses.5:11: I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you shall have no soothsayers.
verses.5:12: I will also cut off your carved images and your sacred pillars from your midst, and you shall no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
verses.5:13: I will uproot your Asherah poles from your midst, and I will destroy your cities.
verses.5:14: And I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations that have not obeyed."
verses.6:1: Hear now what the LORD says: "Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
verses.6:2: Hear, O mountains, the controversy of the LORD, and you enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a controversy with His people, and He will contend with Israel.
verses.6:3: "O My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? Testify against Me!
verses.6:4: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and from the house of bondage I redeemed you; and I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.6:5: O My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD."
verses.6:6: "With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the God on high? Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
verses.6:7: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I offer my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"
verses.6:8: He has declared to you, O man, what is good; and what does the LORD require from you except to practice justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
verses.6:9: The voice of the LORD cries out to the city—and sound wisdom shall see Your name: Hear the rod, and the One who has appointed it!
verses.6:10: "Are there still treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and a scant measure that is accursed?
verses.6:11: Shall I count pure the one with wicked scales, and with a bag of deceitful weights?
verses.6:12: For her rich men are full of violence, her inhabitants speak falsehood, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
verses.6:13: Therefore I also have made you sick by striking you, making you desolate on account of your sins.
verses.6:14: You shall eat, yet you shall not be satisfied, and your hunger shall remain within you; you shall carry away, yet you shall not preserve, and whatever you do preserve I will give over to the sword.
verses.6:15: You shall sow, yet you shall not reap; you shall tread the olives, yet you shall not anoint yourself with oil; and sweet wine, yet you shall not drink wine.
verses.6:16: For the statutes of Omri are diligently kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and you walk in their counsels; therefore I will give you over to desolation, and her inhabitants to hissing, and you shall bear the reproach of My people."
verses.7:1: Woe to me! For I have become like the gatherings of summer fruit, like the gleanings of the vintage; there is no cluster to eat, nor a first-ripe fig that my soul craves.
verses.7:2: The godly man has perished from the land, and there is no upright person among mankind; all of them lie in wait for bloodshed, and every man hunts his brother with a net.
verses.7:3: Both hands are upon evil, to do it skillfully: the prince makes his demand, and the judge asks for a reward; the great man speaks the wicked desire of his soul, and thus they weave it together.
verses.7:4: The best of them is like a brier; the most upright is worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, your visitation, has come; now shall be their confusion.
verses.7:5: Do not trust in a neighbor; do not put confidence in a close friend. Guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom.
verses.7:6: For a son treats his father with contempt, a daughter rises up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.
verses.7:7: But as for me, I will watch for the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
verses.7:8: Do not rejoice over me, O my enemy; though I have fallen, I shall rise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD is a light to me.
verses.7:9: I will endure the indignation of the LORD, for I have sinned against Him, until He pleads my cause and executes justice on my behalf; He will bring me out into the light, and I shall behold His righteousness.
verses.7:10: Then my enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes shall look upon her; now she shall be trampled down like the mire of the streets.
verses.7:11: A day for building your walls—on that day the boundary shall be extended far.
verses.7:12: On that day they shall come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt even to the River, from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
verses.7:13: Yet the earth shall become a desolation because of those who dwell in it, on account of the fruit of their deeds.
verses.7:14: Shepherd Your people with Your staff, the flock of Your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest in the midst of Carmel; let them pasture in Bashan and Gilead, as in days of old.
verses.7:15: As in the days of your coming out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wondrous things.
verses.7:16: The nations shall see and be ashamed because of all their might; they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, and their ears shall grow deaf.
verses.7:17: They shall lick the dust like a serpent; like crawling things of the earth they shall come trembling out of their strongholds; they shall turn in dread to the LORD our God, and they shall be afraid of You.
verses.7:18: Who is a God like You, forgiving iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of His inheritance? He does not keep His anger forever, because He delights in lovingkindness.
verses.7:19: He will again have compassion on us; He will tread our iniquities underfoot, and You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
verses.7:20: You will grant faithfulness to Jacob and lovingkindness to Abraham, which You swore to our fathers from the days of old.

notes.1:3: The Qere and Ketiv differ slightly in the spelling of the construct plural bamotei ("high places of"), without altering the meaning.
notes.1:8: The Qere reads sholal ("barefoot" or "stripped"), whereas the Ketiv reads sheilal; both describe the humbled state of a captive in mourning.
notes.1:10: The Qere reads the imperative hitpallashi ("roll yourself"), whereas the Ketiv reads the first-person form ("I have rolled myself"). This verse launches a sequence of Hebrew wordplays on town names, pairing Beth-le-aphrah ("House of Dust") with "dust."
notes.1:14: The name Achzib plays on the Hebrew word akhzav ("deception," used of a stream that runs dry), continuing Micah's laments over the Judean towns.
notes.2:4: "A bitter lamentation" renders the emphatic Hebrew wordplay nehi nihyah (literally "a wailing of what has come to pass"), stressing total devastation.
notes.2:6: The Hebrew verb nataph literally means "to drip" and is used idiomatically for speaking prophetically or preaching; yissag literally means "shall turn back" or "depart," though some take it as "overtake."
notes.2:12: The Hebrew botsrah means "enclosure" or "sheepfold," though it may alternatively be read as the place name Bozrah, noted for its pastures and flocks.
notes.3:2: The Qere reads the masculine noun ra ("evil"), whereas the Ketiv has the feminine form raah; the meaning is the same.
notes.3:5: "Consecrate war" renders the Hebrew idiom qiddeshu milchamah, referring to the formal proclamation of war accompanied by sacred rites.
notes.3:12: "The mountain of the house" refers to the temple mount in Jerusalem; this exact oracle is later quoted by the elders of the land in Jeremiah 26:18.
notes.4:8: Tower of the flock translates Hebrew Migdal-Eder, and stronghold translates Ophel, both used here as poetic designations of Zion's royal eminence.
notes.4:13: The Masoretic Hebrew reads first-person singular, I will devote, using the verb for setting spoils apart exclusively to the LORD.
notes.4:14: The Hebrew pairs a verb that can mean either muster in troops or gash oneself in mourning with daughter of troops. In many English versions this verse is numbered as 5:1.
notes.5:1: Thousands reflects the Hebrew term denoting both numerical thousands and tribal clans or divisions of Judah. Verses 5:1 through 5:14 follow Masoretic numbering, corresponding to 5:2 through 5:15 in many English versions.
notes.5:5: At its entrances translates the literal Masoretic Hebrew; some interpreters connect the noun with drawn swords by comparison with Psalm 55:21.
notes.6:9: Shall see Your name follows the Masoretic vocalization from the verb meaning to see, though some ancient versions and commentators connect the consonants with fearing the LORD's name.
notes.6:13: Have made you sick translates the Masoretic verb from the root meaning to afflict with sickness, indicating a grievous blow, rather than the variant reading have begun found in some ancient versions.
notes.6:14: Hunger renders a rare Hebrew noun occurring only here in Scripture, denoting inward emptiness or hollowness.
notes.6:16: My people follows the Masoretic Hebrew text directly.
notes.7:3: The Hebrew infinitive literally means to do well or skillfully, used here ironically of practiced wrongdoing; the final verb depicts corrupt leaders weaving their schemes together like a braided cord.
notes.7:11: The Hebrew noun rendered boundary can also mean decree or statute, yielding the alternate sense that an oppressive decree will be far removed.
notes.7:12: The Hebrew term matsor, literally fortress or stronghold, serves here as a poetic name for Egypt, paired with Assyria and the River, meaning the Euphrates.
notes.7:18: The opening question, Who is a God like You, echoes the prophet's own name, Micah, which means Who is like the LORD.
notes.7:19: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts from first-person plural us and our to third-person plural their sins, referring to the remnant of God's inheritance mentioned in the preceding verse.
